t: The meaning of belief in the Qur'an
Entry into Paradise by merely reciting the kalimah
Is the glad tiding of Paradise upon mere faith?
Acting on the commands is the work of high-ranking Muslims
There is no faith alongside denial of the Qur'an or the hadith
s: When I have faith in the Noble Qur'an, what then is the ruling concerning one who denies the whole of the Qur'an Majīd, either entirely or in part, or who denies a portion of the Qur'an Sharīf, either entirely…

Zayd says: although Muslims openly commit sins in the world and carry out deeds of transgression and immorality; such people pray only a few of the prayers and keep only a few of the fasts of Ramadan; they…

Concerning the verse ﴿إِنَّ الَّذِيْنَ اٰمَنُوْا وَعَمِلُوا الصّٰلِحٰتِ كَانَتْ لَهُمْ﴾ etc., a scholar stated that the position of most exegetes is that a mere believer, without righteous deeds — prayer…

Some Muslims say this: that not praying, not giving zakat, not keeping fasts, telling lies, watching films and taking bribes make no difference to an ordinary Muslim; that all these deeds are for first-rank…

Is one who denies the Qur'an Pāk a disbeliever or not? And likewise, is one who denies the prophetic hadiths a disbeliever or not? The questioner notes that the Qur'an says to take whatever the Messenger gives…
k: the meaning of belief in the qur'an when i have faith in the noble qur'an what then is the ruling concerning one who denies the whole of the qur'an majid either entirely or in part or who denies a portion of the qur'an sharif either entirely or in part whether that denial is made with the tongue or through the other limbs complete affirmation of the qur'an pak is obligatory if concerning the whole qur'an or any part of it a verse a person holds the belief that it is not revealed from allah ta'ala then faith does not remain and if the deficiency is in action then it will not be ruled disbelief faith itself is weakened and enfeebled by it but it does not come to an end so long as the affirmation of the heart remains and allah glorified be he knows best

entry into paradise by merely reciting the kalimah zayd says although muslims openly commit sins in the world and carry out deeds of transgression and immorality such people pray only a few of the prayers and keep only a few of the fasts of ramadan they listen to sermons and admonition and yet remain heedless of the rights owed to allah's servants they do not discharge even the rights of inheritance and they disregard the command of allah and his messenger will such people then if at the time of death they recite the kalimah or the kalimah is granted to them go straight into paradise at once without punishment for zayd says that by receiving the kalimah every sin is forgiven and a person enters paradise immediately kindly explain zayd's saying this as a universal rule is not correct otherwise the denial of countless texts will follow however as for the person who has come to faith and after coming to faith has committed no sin concerning him zayd's statement is correct in the qur'an pak it is that is whoever does good equal to an atom's weight will see it and whoever does evil equal to an atom's weight will see it if a person has committed sins in the life of this world and the rights of allah and the rights of his servants stand as obligations upon him then merely reciting the kalimah tayyibah at the time of dying does not bring those rights to an end zayd must repent of this statement of his because this statement of his is against the qur'an pak the hadith sharif and the consensus of the ummah for the rest this much is certainly established that whoever recited the kalimah tayyibah at the final moment that is whose end came upon faith for him there is the promise of paradise and he will certainly go to paradise but that every person goes into paradise at once and without reckoning is neither promised nor established anywhere rather some people will go into paradise without reckoning some will go after their punishment has been carried out in full some will go by means of intercession some will be brought out of hell by the permission of the prophet and some allah ta'ala will bring out himself some will be taken out of hell in such a state that they have been burnt and turned entirely black like charcoal and all of these will be those whose end came upon faith all of this is mentioned in bukhari sharif and in many other books of hadith

is the glad tiding of paradise upon mere faith concerning the verse etc a scholar stated that the position of most exegetes is that a mere believer without righteous deeds prayer fasting and so on is also deserving of this glad tiding because a thing is not conjoined to itself how is this in itself if a person dies as soon as he brings faith and the occasion for righteous deeds did not arise then he too is included in this glad tiding under the law of allah on the basis of being upon the true religion and as for one who after bringing faith was given time but performed no righteous deeds and instead remained caught up in acts of disobedience for him entry is not forbidden as a matter of law but he will be deserving of paradise after punishment what this scholar's own argument yields is that faith and righteous deeds are separate from one another therefore the glad tiding will be upon the combination of the two not upon faith alone so to present this as proof that a mere believer deserves the glad tiding will be wrong and allah knows best

acting on the commands is the work of high ranking muslims some muslims say this that not praying not giving zakat not keeping fasts telling lies watching films and taking bribes make no difference to an ordinary muslim that all these deeds are for first rank muslims to perform and there is no need for us to perform them because we are only ordinary muslims that allah ta'ala is most forgiving and most merciful and we have complete conviction that he will surely forgive us and we will surely go to paradise is this correct and what is the ruling concerning those who say such a thing the real most high is forgiving and merciful and he is also ever subduing and the avenger he made paradise and he made hell as well he also sent down the commands and he appointed paradise for those who obey to accept one attribute of allah ta'ala and not to accept another attribute is not a matter of faith as for the things he has forbidden abstaining from them is obligatory in the same way that they think the commands are for first rank muslims to carry out and that we are only ordinary muslims they ought also to have thought this might it not be that paradise too is for first rank muslims and that for those people who do not act there is hell therefore such a statement such a belief and such conduct guarding fully against them is obligatory otherwise slowly faith and islam all of these things come to an end and allah glorified be he knows best

there is no faith alongside denial of the qur'an or the hadith is one who denies the qur'an pak a disbeliever or not and likewise is one who denies the prophetic hadiths a disbeliever or not the questioner notes that the qur'an says to take whatever the messenger gives and to abstain from whatever he forbids al hashr 7 so if a person denies the hadiths is that not against this verse and the qur'an says that he does not speak from desire that it is only revelation revealed al najm 3 4 of what then would this be said further how was it even known that a thing is in the qur'an when he has denied the hadiths for the hadith warns against the man reclining on his couch who when a command or prohibition of the prophet reaches him says 'i do not know whatever we find in the book of allah that we follow' and the prophet said that he was given the qur'an and its like along with it one who finds fault with the blessed person of the prophet or with any one of his lofty attributes is a disbeliever whether the one who does so is a muslim a dhimmi or a harbi and even if he did it by way of jest he is liable to execution and his repentance is not accepted there is consensus of the ummah that disrespect and contempt toward any prophet is disbelief and that it is forbidden for the one who commits it to regard it as lawful as for the denial of hadith the number of the rak'ahs of prayer is not established from the qur'an and in the same way the details of zakat are not set out there there are a great many rulings whose particulars are not found in the qur'an is the one who denies these then not a disbeliever and it is stated in the kamalayn that because the prophet's journey to bayt al maqdis is established by a definitive text the one who denies it is a disbeliever so denial of what is definitively established from the messenger stands on the same footing as denial of the qur'an itself since the greater part of the detail of the shari'ah reaches us only by way of the sunnah
